batch: INOD and CTAS (the operator's request, 2026-10-28): CTAS

runs.name: Cintas Corporation; Nasdaq CTAS, Washington, 10-K filer; uniform rental and facility services, first aid and safety, fire protection; signed 2026-03-10 to buy UniFirst for cash and stock, not closed
runs.box: OUT AT Q7, ON PRICE; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: A fresh v5 run at the operator's request ("Run innodata and cintas"), replacing the run of 2026-10-07 as the run of record; interactive dispatch under the canonical brief, two analysts in parallel, lock held by the main session; the brief's one departure is the repository path after the move of 2026-10-25. Price **$214.80** (2026-10-27, aggregator, flagged) x **397,075,093 shares** (one class, 10-Q cover `0000723254-26-000047`) = cap **$85,292M**; sovereign **5.30%** (Treasury 30-year, 2026-10-27). Q1 IN (about 12,500 routes, more than a million business customers, none above 1% of revenue; over 95% route-service fees). Q2 IN: Uniform Rental and Facility Services decides at 80.9% of FY2022 to FY2026 segment profit; its margin 17.9% (FY2016) to 24.1% (FY2026), rising through the COVID volume fall, so the change for the better is credited; the low-cost operator in a commodity-like field; rivals' margins fell over the span (UniFirst 13.7% to 5.4%; Aramark Uniform then Vestis 12.5% to 2.4% with a net loss). Q3 for (pre-tax return on capital excluding goodwill 69.8% in FY2026; added capital FY2021 to FY2026 earned 134% excluding goodwill, 79% including). Q4 for (clean accounts; adjusted-EPS guidance and an EBITDA-multiple merger price carried to Q5). Q5 integrity IN, ability for. Q6 against (about $6.7B of buybacks since FY2017 with no stated price, shares only 416.9M to 397.1M; buybacks at $179 to $200, above the top of the range). UniFirst: $275 cash proposed January 2025, talks ended March 2025, renewed December 2025, merger signed 2026-03-10 at $155 cash plus 0.7720 Cintas shares (about $5.5B), holders approved, an FTC second request, no closing before 2026-12-11; Q6's all-stock STOP does not fire (Cintas stock above value; half cash). Q7 OUT on price: owner cash (acquisitions deducted) $1,382.4M a year all-equity, $1,303.8M equity-only (FY2022 to FY2026), growing 10.69% a year against revenue at 9.43%; range **$63.34 to $174.26 a share all-equity (central)** at the sovereign, 2.75 to one; the price above the top, and the most generous case earns 4.47% at the price, below the bond; equity-only $66.37 to $179.48, organic pair $66.33 to $157.23, literal window $58.92 to $147.79, UniFirst as if closed $56.50 to $166.74; fair price **$52.49 all-equity** ($57.66 equity-only; $45.36 with UniFirst as if closed, no synergies). Integrity facts recorded, not judged: City of Laurel v. Cintas (public agencies' contract claims) settled for $45.0M; pay on EPS and sales growth with no capital charge; a jointly owned airplane with the Farmer family, a brother-in-law on the board, a related-party policy "not in written form". Replaces the alert of the 2026-10-07 run ($51.72, restated 2026-10-10). Dispatcher's check: check_framework PASS; pathspec commits, own paths only. Contamination declared: commit subjects, `git status` names, the name `PORTFOLIO.md`; none opened. Position note filled at the fold: not held. Armed at the all-equity fair price.
runs.narr: OUT at Q7 on price: the best business of this week's runs (a low-cost route network whose margins widened while both rivals' collapsed, about 70% pre-tax on capital), priced above the top of its value range and below the bond on every case. Range $63.34 to $174.26 all-equity vs $214.80, fair $52.49. Buying UniFirst at about $5.5B on synergies, and buying back its own stock above value.
runs.fair_label: CTAS v5 fair price, all-equity central, the run of 2026-10-28 (replacing the 2026-10-07 run's $51.72): owner cash $1,382.4M a year with acquisitions deducted; $45.36 with UniFirst as if closed, beside; a prompt for a full re-run, never a buy
